# swift-nostr

> A modern Swift toolkit for Nostr protocol: the shared `NostrCore` primitives, the high-level, multi-relay `NostrClient` built on them, `NostrWalletConnect` for NIP-47 payments, and `NostrConnect` for NIP-46 remote signing. Actor-based concurrency, NIP-44 encryption, NIP-59 gift wrap, and BIP-39 key derivation. MIT licensed, requires Swift 6.3+.

The high-level `NostrClient` library provides an actor-based API for the Nostr network, built on the `NostrCore` primitives:

- `NostrClient` actor: relay management, event publishing, subscriptions, fetches, direct messages. Its API is reached through eight feature namespaces — `client.identity`, `client.relays`, `client.events`, `client.subscriptions`, `client.routing`, `client.messages`, `client.groups`, `client.lists` — each a `Sendable` façade conforming to a capability protocol (`NostrIdentityProviding`, `NostrRelayManaging`, `NostrEventPublishing`, `NostrEventFetching`, `NostrSubscribing`, `NostrRelayRouting`, `NostrMessaging`, `NostrGroupManaging`, `NostrListManaging`) so a feature can depend on one slice. `NostrClient` itself exposes only its initializers and these namespaces.
- `KeyPair` / `PublicKey` / `EventSigner`: key generation, import (hex/nsec/mnemonic), event signing
- `EventTemplate`: what an event's author decides (kind, tags, content, `createdAt`; mutable before signing), built by static factories — `.textNote(_:tags:)`, `.reply(to:content:relayURL:)` (NIP-10 threading), `.reaction(to:content:)`, `.repost(of:relayURL:)`, `.deletion(of:reason:)`, `.clientAuthentication(relayURL:challenge:)`, `.zapRequest(to:relays:amountMillisats:lnurl:eventID:eventCoordinate:comment:)`, the NIP-29 `.groupJoinRequest(groupID:inviteCode:reason:)`, `.groupLeaveRequest(groupID:reason:)`, `.groupContent(groupID:kind:content:tags:previous:)`, and `.groupModeration(_:groupID:previous:reason:)`, the NIP-98 `.httpAuthorization(url:method:payload:)`, and in NostrClient `.metadata(_:)`, `.contactList(_:)`, `.relayListMetadata(_:)`, `.directMessageRelayList(_:)`, `.report(_:type:reason:)`, `.longFormContent(_:draft:)`, and the NIP-51 `.list(_:encryptingWith:)` / `.set(_:encryptingWith:)` (private items NIP-44-encrypted to the signer, read back with `NostrList(event:decryptingWith:)` / `NostrListSet(event:decryptingWith:)`) — and signed with `signer.sign(_:)` (`try signer.sign(.textNote("gm"))` on a local `EventSigner`, `try await` on any `NostrSigning`); `sign(_:proofOfWork:)` mines it to a NIP-13 difficulty first
- `NostrSigning`: signer abstraction over `EventSigner` (local key) and `RemoteSigner` (NIP-46) for signing + NIP-44; `client.identity.setSigner(_:)` accepts either, and every client feature runs through it — `identity.sign(_:)` (an `EventTemplate`), `identity.nip44Encrypt(_:to:)`/`nip44Decrypt(_:from:)`, `events.publish(_:)` (an `EventTemplate`, signed first, or a signed `Event`), the convenience `publish*` helpers, NIP-17 direct messages, NIP-51 private list items, and NIP-42 auth all work with either signer
- `EncryptedPrivateKey`: NIP-49 password-encrypted private keys (`ncryptsec`), scrypt + XChaCha20-Poly1305
- `Event` / `Filter` / `SubscriptionEvent`: NIP-01 data models; an event's `id`, `publicKey` (the `pubkey` field), and `signature` (the `sig` field, `nil` for an unsigned NIP-59 rumor) are the typed `EventID`, `PublicKey`, and `Signature`, each holding only canonical lowercase hex; `Filter`, the `Tag` builders, `NostrSigning`, `EventSigner`, NIP-29 `Groups`, `RelayMessage.ok`, every `NostrClient` API and model (`client.identity.publicKey`, NIP-19 entities, contacts, direct messages, routing, lists, groups, zaps, NIP-05), and the NIP-46/NIP-47 sessions and connection URIs (`RemoteSigner`, `BunkerURI`, `NostrConnectURI`, `WalletConnectURI`) take and return these typed values, and accessors over third-party data (`referencedEventIDs`, `referencedPublicKeys`, contact lists, NIP-11 `publicKey`, LNURL `nostrPublicKey`, NIP-05 `nostr.json`, zap receipt tags) skip or drop values that are not canonical hex
- `Timestamp`: whole Unix seconds as on the wire (a bare JSON number), used by `Event.createdAt`, `EventTemplate.createdAt`, `UnsignedEvent.createdAt`, `Filter.since`/`until`, NIP-40 `Tag.expiration` / `Event.expiration` / `isExpired(asOf:)`, direct message `createdAt`/`expiresAt` and every `expiration:` parameter, `LongFormContent.publishedAt`, `client.groups.timeline(_:kinds:since:limit:)`, `Bolt11Invoice.timestamp`, and NIP-47 transaction times and `list_transactions` `from`/`until`; `Timestamp(date)` and `.date` clamp out-of-range values instead of trapping, and `advanced(by:)` / `duration(to:)` do `Duration` arithmetic in whole seconds without going through `Date`
- `Duration` for every period: `RelayConnectionConfig` timeouts, ping interval, and reconnect delays, `RelayPoolConfig.deduplicationCacheTTL` and `queryTimeout`, the per-call `timeout:` of one-shot fetches and counts (`nil` uses `queryTimeout`), `RemoteSigner.Config` and `WalletConnection.Config` timeouts, the `HTTPAuth.validate` `tolerance:`, `Bolt11Invoice.expiry`, NIP-47 `MakeInvoiceParams.expiry`, the NIP-11 `created_at` limits (relative offsets), fee `period`, and retention `time`; the wire formats keep integer seconds
- `RelayURL`: a validated `ws`/`wss` relay URL in canonical form (lowercased scheme and host, no root slash or default port), equal across spellings; every relay-taking or relay-returning API uses it — pool membership and lookup, publish/fetch/count/subscribe targets, `PublishResult`, `expectedRelays`, `SubscriptionEvent.relayURL`, NIP-42 auth, tag relay hints, NIP-65 and NIP-17 relay lists, NIP-19 relay hints, NIP-29 group references, NIP-05 relays, zap requests, and the `bunker://` / `nostrconnect://` / `nostr+walletconnect://` URIs; relay URLs read from other people's data are parsed leniently (a malformed one is skipped), while a connection URI with a malformed relay fails to parse
- `RelayPool` / `RelayConnection`: multi-relay WebSocket management with auto-reconnect
- `DirectMessage` / `DirectMessageReaction` / `DirectMessageFile` / `DirectMessagePayload` / `DirectMessageBuilder` / `DirectMessageParser`: NIP-17 private DMs, NIP-25 reactions, and kind 15 file messages; `client.messages.sendGiftWrapped(_:to:)` delivers a rumor of any kind the same way
- `EncryptedFile`: AES-256-GCM encryption for NIP-17 file messages
- `Groups` / `GroupReference` / `GroupState`: NIP-29 relay-based groups — join/leave and chat with timeline references (events built by the `EventTemplate.group*` factories), moderation (kinds 9000-9002, 9005, 9007-9010), relay-signed state parsing (metadata/admins/members/roles/pins), naddr share links with invite codes
- `SimpleGroupList` / `GroupListEntry`: the NIP-51 kind-10009 list of the NIP-29 groups a user is in (public + NIP-44-encrypted private entries)
- `SealedMessage` / `GiftWrap`: NIP-44 encryption and NIP-59 gift wrap
- `LNURL` / `LNURLPayResponse`: NIP-57 zap LNURL-pay resolution and invoice-request URLs
- `Mnemonic` / `KeyDerivation`: BIP-39 seed phrase and BIP-32 key derivation (NIP-06)

## Supported NIPs

- NIP-01: Basic protocol (events, filters, subscriptions)
- NIP-02: Contact list and petnames
- NIP-03: OpenTimestamps attestations
- NIP-05: DNS-based internet identifiers
- NIP-06: BIP-39 key derivation
- NIP-09: Event deletion
- NIP-10: Reply threading (root/reply markers)
- NIP-11: Relay information document
- NIP-13: Proof of work (leading-zero-bit difficulty, mining, validation)
- NIP-17: Private direct messages (kind 10050 DM relay lists, kind 15 encrypted file messages)
- NIP-18: Reposts
- NIP-19: bech32-encoded entities (npub, nsec, note, nprofile, nevent, naddr)
- NIP-20: Command results (OK)
- NIP-21: nostr: URI scheme
- NIP-23: Long-form content (kind 30023 articles, kind 30024 drafts)
- NIP-25: Reactions (incl. private DM reactions)
- NIP-27: Text note references (nostr: mentions and quotes in content)
- NIP-29: Relay-based groups (join/leave, chat with timeline references, moderation kinds 9000-9002, 9005, 9007-9010, relay-signed state parsing, naddr share links with invite codes)
- NIP-40: Expiration timestamp (disappearing messages)
- NIP-42: Client authentication (automatic challenge response, auth-required retry)
- NIP-44: Versioned encryption (v2)
- NIP-45: Event counts (COUNT)
- NIP-46: Nostr Connect (remote signing; bunker:// and client-initiated nostrconnect:// flows, auth_url challenges, typed commands — separate `NostrConnect` library)
- NIP-47: Nostr Wallet Connect (full command set, NIP-44/NIP-04 encryption, notifications — separate `NostrWalletConnect` library)
- NIP-49: Private key encryption (ncryptsec)
- NIP-50: Search capability
- NIP-51: Lists (standard lists + parameterized sets; NIP-44-encrypted private items; kind-10009 simple group list)
- NIP-56: Reporting (kind 1984)
- NIP-57: Lightning Zaps (zap request kind 9734, LNURL helpers, invoice fetch, bolt11 decoding, kind-9735 receipt validation)
- NIP-59: Gift wrap
- NIP-65: Relay list metadata (outbox model)

## Requirements

- Swift 6.3+
- iOS 17.0+ / macOS 14.0+ / tvOS 17.0+ / watchOS 10.0+ / visionOS 1.0+
- MIT License
